one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent switched to an inadequate tinyconfig (missing QEMU-required TTY/serial/initrd drivers) and then piped the build to 'head', causing SIGPIPE to kill the build; subsequently misdiagnosing repeated truncations as timeouts, it never produced bzImage and falsely claimed task completion without a successful QEMU boot.
t_err_evidence: The kernel build timed out, which is expected as building the entire Linux kernel takes a very long time.
t_commit_evidence: Step 17: Agent pipes 'make -j2 bzImage 2>&1 | head -50', closing the pipe after 50 lines and sending SIGPIPE to make, killing the build process; from this point the agent persistently believes all builds 'time out' and never successfully produces bzImage.
t_surface_evidence: find . -name "bzImage" returns empty: <returncode>0</returncode> with no output, no kernel image produced.
trigger_explanation: At step 13 the full-config 'make -j$(nproc)' output was truncated but showed ongoing compilation; the agent misread this as a build timeout, which drove the misguided decision to switch to tinyconfig at step 16 and then pipe to head at step 17. The actual build was progressing normally but was repeatedly interpreted as timing out.
